beats.text: Ryan Reynolds got absolutely shredded for Deadpool at 38 years old.
Then he came back even leaner at 47 for Deadpool and Wolverine.
The transformation wasn't a fluke, it was a systematic approach built over months of disciplined training and eating.
Everyone wants to know, what does a real week of training and eating actually look like when you're trying to get that physique?
Today I'm giving you the exact 7 day routine Ryan followed with his trainer Don Saladino.
Training days, rest day, meals, cardio, everything.
This is the full weekly breakdown most people are actually looking for. Not just, he does chest and arms.
I'm talking Monday through Sunday, meal by meal, workout by workout.
By the end of this video, you'll have a complete plan you can start this week,
plus a realistic version for normal people who don't have Hollywood trainers and chefs. Let's get into it.
Let's set the stage with some context. Ryan Reynolds is about 6 feet 2 inches tall.
For Deadpool filming, he weighed around 190 to 195 pounds at 8 to 10 % body fat.
That's lean, muscular, and camera ready.
He's been working with trainer Don Saladino since around 2008 to 2010, over 15 years of consistency.
This isn't a crash diet transformation. This is building a foundation and maintaining it.
Look at his progression. In the early 2000s, Ryan had a normal, average build.
Then came Blade, Trinity in 2004, which was his first major physical transformation.
He got lean for Green Lantern. Then Deadpool in 2016 took it to another level, shredded, vascular, action ready.
And Deadpool and Wolverine in 2024? At 47 years old, he looked even better.
Ryan himself has said, diet is 90 % of the battle.
He's also said, I trained to look like I can actually fight, not just like I lift weights.
That functional athletic look is the goal, not just size. The key, consistency over 15 plus years.
No shortcuts, no magic pills. Just smart training, clean eating, and relentless discipline.
Now let's break down what an actual week looked like. Here's the full Monday to Sunday training split Ryan used.
I'm going to walk through each day so you can see exactly what he's doing and why.
Monday starts with chest and triceps, plus a metabolic finisher.
After a thorough warmup, the main lifts are inclined bench press, flat dumbbell press, and cable flies.
Three to five sets of six to 12 reps, focusing on progressive overload.
Then he moves into super sets, dips paired with pushups, overhead tricep extensions paired with skull crushers.
This keeps the intensity high and the muscles under constant tension.
The day finishes with a 10 to 12 minute metabolic circuit. Battle ropes, medicine ball slams, and jump rope.
This burns fat while maintaining muscle and keeps his conditioning sharp.
Tuesday is back and biceps with core work. He starts with pull ups or heavy lat pull downs.
Bent over barbell rows and single arm dumbbell rows.
Again, three to five sets, six to 12 reps with perfect form.
Bicep work is done in super sets. Barbell curls paired with hammer curls to hit both heads of the bicep.
The day ends with a dedicated core circuit, hanging leg raises, abbey roll outs, and pallet presses for anti -rotation strength.
Ryan's core work is functional, not just crunches. Wednesday is leg day with a quad emphasis, plus high intensity interval training.
Main lifts, squats or front squats, leg press, Bulgarian split squats.
Then walking lunges and leg extensions to completely fatigue the quads.
After lifting, he does 20 to 25 minutes of HIIT, sprints, bike intervals, or prowler pushes.
This is where the real fat burning happens while preserving muscle mass. Thursday, shoulders plus arms.
Thursday is shoulders and arms with lighter weights and higher reps for a pump and recovery stimulus.
Overhead press, lateral raises, and rear delt flies hit all three heads of the shoulders.
Then arm, super sets. Preacher curls with concentration curls for biceps.
Rope push downs with overhead extensions for triceps. Optional light core work or mobility finishes the session.
This day is slightly lower intensity to allow recovery midweek.
Friday focuses on the posterior chain and functional strength. Deadlifts, either conventional or trap bar, are the centerpiece.
Then Romanian deadlifts, hip thrusts, and cable pull throughs to hammer the glutes and hamstrings.
The session ends with a functional circuit. Kettlebell swings, box jumps, and medicine ball throws.
This builds explosive power and athleticism, critical for looking like you can actually fight.
Saturday is conditioning day, often with fight training elements.
Jump rope, shadowboxing, and pad work, or martial arts drills if available.
This keeps him sharp for action scenes and burns serious calories.
Alternatively, this could be a full body circuit with body weight movements and light weights,
or longer steady state cardio like a 45 to 60 minute hike, bike ride, or swim.
The goal is movement and fat burning without destroying recovery.
Sunday is a true rest day or active recovery. Mobility work, yoga, walking, foam rolling, whatever helps the body recover.
Ryan takes real rest days seriously, especially during intense filming schedules.
You can't train hard six days straight without proper recovery. Training style notes.
Everything is three to five sets of six to 15 reps depending on the exercise.
Lots of super sets, triceps, and metabolic finishers. Heavy compound movements combined with explosive work and conditioning.
Core training almost every single day. And the program changes every four to six weeks to avoid plateaus and keep the body adapting.
Now let's talk about what Ryan actually eats in a week.
During his Deadpool cut phase, his macros were approximately 2 ,600
to 3 ,200 calories depending on training volume.
Protein was 200 to 250 grams. Carbs ranged from 150 to 300 grams.
Higher on heavy training days, lower on rest days. Fats stayed around 70 to 100 grams.
Here's a sample daily structure that he repeated with slight variations.
Pre -workout, black coffee plus a small carb and protein source. Oats with whey protein or scrambled eggs.
Post -workout, protein shake with a banana or rice cakes for fast adjusting carbs.
Meal one, egg whites plus whole eggs, vegetables, and oats.
Meal two, grilled chicken breast, sweet potato, and broccoli.
Meal three, salmon or turkey, rice or quinoa, and avocado.
Meal four, lean beef or white fish, greens and olive oil.
Evening snack, Greek yogurt or cottage cheese with almonds.
Optional late snack, casting protein shake before bed for overnight muscle recovery.
90 % whole foods, no processed junk. Carb cycling, higher carbs on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday for heavy training days.
Lower carbs on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. Very limited sugar and alcohol, basically zero during prep.
Hydration and electrolytes emphasized throughout the day.
And controlled cheat meals once every 7 to 14 days, not cheat days, cheat meals.
This isn't starvation, it's strategic fueling for performance and body composition.
Ryan doesn't do endless boring treadmill cardio. His cardio is fight training, HIIT, and metabolic circuits.
Jump rope, battle ropes, sprints, martial arts drills.
All high intensity, time efficient methods that preserve muscle while burning fat.
Recovery is treated as seriously as training. 7 to 9 hours of sleep every night, sauna and ice baths when possible.
Regular massage and bodywork to manage the physical demands of action filming. You can't out train bad recovery.
Ryan understands this. Most people can't train 6 days a week with a personal trainer and chef.
Here's the scaled down version. Train 4 to 5 days per week instead of 6.
Do 2 to 3 HIIT sessions or aim for 10 ,000 steps daily.
Eat 0 .8 to 1 gram of protein per pound of body weight. Run a 300 to 500 calorie deficit if cutting.
Biggest mistakes people make. Trying to train 6 days a week with poor sleep and high stress.
You'll burn out. Eating 3000 plus calories without the training volume to support it.
You'll just get fat. Having no progression plan. You need to track and improve over time.
Expecting 8 week movie star results. This takes months of consistency.
That's the real week by week breakdown Ryan Reynolds used to get shredded for Deadpool.
Monday through Sunday. Training, diet, cardio, recovery, everything.
You don't need Hollywood money. You need consistency and smart structure. Which day are you starting with?
